title: 03 — Backend API (client guide)
tagline: What the app calls on the backend, what it sends and gets back, how each call works on the server, and what the app must do with the answer.

series.name: SiteLog: an iOS app and its API, built

intro: What the app calls on the backend, what it sends and gets back, how each call works on the server, and what the app must do with the answer.
The backend lives in its own repository: site-log-be. Full contract with every field and example: site-log-be · 01-api. Server internals, AWS and the backend guides: site-log-be docs.
Client side of uploads, sync and realtime: 02-upload-sync.md.

RuleDetail
Auth headerAuthorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>; get it with getIDToken(forcingRefresh: false) on every request, never cache it yourself
BodyJSON, Content-Type: application/json, ≤ 1 MiB
NamescamelCase fields
IdsApp-made UUIDs; the server returns them lowercase — compare with UUID(uuidString:), not as strings
TimestampsISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds 2026-11-05T09:00:00.000Z: ISO8601DateFormatter with [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]
DatesYYYY-MM-DD
HashesSHA-256, 64 lowercase hex
ClockThe Date header of any response (e.g. /health) is the trusted time for the clock offset
  • Where it is built: PlatformKit/Networking (HTTPClient, base URL and token provider through init); each feature's remote data source in DataLayer/DataSources/Remote/ maps DTOs.

blocks.html:
• Every route except /health and /verify runs requireUser on the server: verifyIdToken(token, checkRevoked: true) → the caller's uid, or 401.
  • Every file key and row is scoped to that uid; the app never sends a uid in a body.
DELETE /account
→ 200 { "deletedObjects": 214, "abortedUploads": 1, "deletedRows": 932 }
Server does, in orderClient rule
Aborts unfinished multipart uploads, deletes every object under {uid}/, deletes every row in one transaction, deletes the Firebase userReauthenticate first; show the numbers; then wipe local store, Keychain and media
Safe to repeat; a repeat returns zerosAfter success the token is revoked: any further call is 401 — sign out locally

blocks.html:
6.1 Pull

POST /sync/pull { "since": <nextRev of last pull, 0 at first>, "limit": 500 }
→ { "changes": { "<table>": [rows] }, "nextRev": 41, "hasMore": false }
→ { "resyncRequired": true }
Server mechanismClient rule
Every row has a per-user rev, gap-free and commit-orderedStore nextRev only after the page is applied
Returns rows with rev > since, tombstones included (deletedAt set)Delete tombstoned rows locally
hasMore: true when cappedPull again at once
resyncRequired when since is older than the 90-day tombstone purgeWipe synced data, pull from 0

6.2 Push

POST /sync/push { "mutations": [ { "table", "id", "op": "upsert" or "delete", "clientUpdatedAt", "fields": { full row } } ] }
→ { "results": [ { "id", "status": "applied" | "superseded" | "rejected", "serverRow"?, "reason"? } ], "serverRev": 44 }
Server mechanismClient rule
One transaction per batch (≤ 200), parents may come after children inside itQueue in dependency order: projects → locations → plan_sheets → sessions → captures → issues → issue_captures → annotations → checklist_*
Last write wins on clientUpdatedAt, decided in SQLSend the time of the edit, not of the push
upsert needs the full row (every field, null where empty)Never send partial fields
A deleted row never comes back; sessions.state only moves forward; frozen columns keep their first valuesuperseded is not an error: adopt serverRow (its id may differ for natural-key tables)
rejected + reason (invalid_row:<code>, missing_parent, forbidden, unknown_field:<name>)Drop that mutation, log the reason, keep the rest

blocks.html:
7.1 Keys

FileKey
Capture{uid}/{projectId}/{sessionId}/{captureId}.{jpg·heic·png·mov·mp4·m4a}
Plan sheet{uid}/{projectId}/plans/{sheetId}.{pdf·jpg·png·heic}
Branding logo{uid}/branding/{logoId}.{png·jpg}
  • Any other shape or another uid → 400 invalid_key.

7.2 Begin and PUT

POST /uploads { "key", "byteSize", "contentType", "sha256" }
→ { "mode": "single", "uploadId", "url", "expiresAt" }
→ { "mode": "multipart", "uploadId", "partSizeBytes": 8388608, "parts": [ { "number", "url" } ], "expiresAt" }   (F07)
Server mechanismClient rule
Picks the mode from byteSize (< 5 MiB single)Never choose the mode yourself; plan parts from partSizeBytes
URLs are signed for 1 hour and include Content-TypePUT with header Content-Type = the contentType sent; keep each part's ETag
Rate limit 600 begins / minute / user429 → back off

7.3 Complete

POST /uploads/:id/complete {}                                   (single)
POST /uploads/:id/complete { "parts": [ { "number", "etag" } ] } (multipart: every part, once)
→ { "uploadId", "remoteKey", "sha256", "verificationCode", "verified": false, "receivedAt" }
Server mechanismClient rule
Locks the upload row, checks the object in S3 (HeadObject, size = byteSize), issues a codeRetry freely: the answer is the same every time (idempotent)
404 object_not_found (nothing uploaded), 400 size_mismatchPermanent: restart the job from the file
The hash is registered now; a worker re-reads the file later and marks it verified (F15)Print "registered {code}" until the channel or a pull says verified

7.4 Refresh, abort, media

CallServerClient
POST /uploads/:id/parts/refresh { "numbers": [13, 14] }New URLs for exactly those parts; 404 once completed or abortedMandatory after a long kill or any S3 403
DELETE /uploads/:idAborts in S3, frees parts; repeatableUser cancel, account switch
POST /media/urls { "keys": [...] } (≤ 200)GET URLs for the caller's own keys, 1 hourKingfisher cache key = the object key, not the URL

GET /verify/K7M2QX9HTP      (no token)
→ { "code", "sha256", "byteSize", "receivedAt", "verifyState": "registered" | "verified" | "mismatch", "verified", "verifiedAt", "projectRef" }
  • Server: public, rate limited per IP, constant delay, never returns the file, a URL, the uid or coordinates.
  • App: print projectRef (first 8 of the project id, upper case) in the report header and the code under each photo; wording per 01-field-work §12.5.

blocks.html:
POST /devices { "token": "<APNs hex>", "environment": "sandbox" | "production" }   → { "registered": true }
DELETE /devices/:token                                                          → { "removed": true }
  • Register after sign-in and on every token change; remove on sign-out. Debug = sandbox, TestFlight and App Store = production.
  • The server pushes once when the last upload of a session is verified: aps.alert, deepLink (sitelog://session/<id>), account (hash of the uid — ignore if it is not the signed-in user).
